Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly prepared to make a 'significant' effort to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela.

Varela has already passed that tally during his short time in Italy, having scored 11 goals in as many competitive matches for Monza.

In fact, he currently leads Serie A's scoring charts with nine goals, including five goals in the club's last five league games before the international window.

Liverpool are among those who have already been linked with a potential swoop for the in-form striker.

Tottenham Hotspur are also in the mix, with Il Giorno reporting the North London club are willing to pay a 'significant' fee to win the race for Varela's signature.

Meanwhile, Benfica have the opportunity to match any offer for Varela, which was a clause included as part of the agreement that saw him join Monza.

#1592. Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers manager with immediate effect due to health reasons - two years after bowel cancer battle forced him to leave Birmingham City

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health issues at Birmingham City.

The veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he said. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'

Speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he says. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood said: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he shows for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'

#1589. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are currently considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

The report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are currently viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

Albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

Despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

#1587. Liverpool vs. Man Utd: How to watch, date, time, live stream, TV channel

By Saikat Mandal | 21 Nov 2026 15:08

Two of the Premier League's most successful clubs renew their fierce rivalry on Sunday as Liverpool welcome Manchester United to Anfield for their first meeting of the season.

The Reds are navigating a period of transition under Andoni Iraola, but have made an encouraging start to the campaign, climbing to fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points.

Manchester United, meanwhile, have endured their worst start to a new season, prompting the club hierarchy to part ways with Michael Carrick, who guided them into the Champions League places last term.

The Red Devils have wasted little time in appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his successor, but the Argentine faces a daunting introduction to the rivalry, having won just three of his 19 managerial meetings with Liverpool.

Here, Sports Mole provides everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Liverpool vs Man Utd is one of two Premier League fixtures scheduled for Sunday, with the other seeing Hull City welcome Brighton & Hove Albion.

The eagerly anticipated clash at Anfield is scheduled to get underway at 4.30pm UK time, a prime Sunday afternoon slot that should allow supporters both in the stands and watching from around the world to savour one of English football's biggest rivalries.

Liverpool vs Man Utd will take place at Anfield, the 61,276-capacity stadium that has served as the spiritual home of the mighty Reds since 1892.

Anfield is the fifth-largest football stadium in England and has been the setting for countless memorable encounters between these fierce rivals, with its famous atmosphere often adding another layer of intensity.

Beyond football, the iconic venue also opens its doors to major musical events during the off-season, with global superstar Taylor Swift among the big-name artists to have performed there during her record-breaking Eras Tour.

Non-Sky customers can stream the contest through a NOW Day or cancel-anytime Month pass, while viewers in India can catch the action live on JioHotstar.

Liverpool and Man Utd's official X accounts are expected to share match snippets throughout the contest, while journalists covering the game may also post their own footage and updates.

After the final whistle, extended highlights should be available on both clubs' official YouTube channels, while viewers in the UK can catch the action again on BBC's Match of the Day 2.

Liverpool have an opportunity to cut the gap to Manchester City to just one point with victory on Sunday, giving them an added incentive to make home advantage count.

The Reds have endured an uncomfortable run against their fiercest rivals at Anfield, having failed to beat the Red Devils on home soil since their emphatic 7-0 triumph in March 2023, and Iraola will be desperate to put that unwanted sequence behind them by claiming all three points.

The likes of Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz will be eager to rise to the occasion and deliver on a stage of such magnitude, but Liverpool's overriding priority is to turn their home performances into consistent results and strengthen their position in the title race.

For Man Utd, the stakes are arguably even higher, with the visitors desperate to climb out of the relegation zone and give their troubled campaign some much-needed impetus.

Pochettino, meanwhile, will be keen to mark the beginning of his Man Utd tenure with a statement victory, although he could hardly have been handed a more demanding opening assignment; given the circumstances, even a hard-earned draw at Anfield would represent a respectable start to his reign.

#1586. Barcelona targeting January move for Tottenham Hotspur defender

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.

According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.

The Catalan club have been dealing with a series of defensive injuries involving Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart. However, Barcelona have not made a final decision on whether to bring in another defender, with the club waiting to assess the injured players’ recoveries.

Laporta’s admiration for Porro reportedly grew during Spain’s World Cup campaign. The Tottenham defender became an important part of the national team, developing a strong understanding with Lamine Yamal on the right flank and scoring twice during the tournament, including in the semi-final against France.

Laporta watched that semi-final in Dallas and was reportedly impressed by Porro’s performance. Barcelona had also gathered information about the defender towards the end of the previous summer transfer window, but their enquiry did not progress into a formal proposal to either the player or Tottenham.

Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

Reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

Barcelona’s admiration for Porro is a reminder of the defender’s standing in European football, but there is currently no confirmed bid or formal approach.

Tottenham will be keen to retain a player who remains an important part of their plans. His long-term contract also means the club are under no immediate pressure to negotiate a sale.

The situation could develop if Barcelona decide their defensive injury problems require January reinforcements. For now, however, Spurs remain in a strong position, and any interested club would likely have to make a substantial offer to test their resolve.
